slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: A practical agent workflow: PM, engineer, QA
slides.subtitle: Use roles, criteria, and loops to improve output quality.

slides.title: PM grooms
slides.body: The PM makes the issue concrete: goal, acceptance criteria, edge cases, and out-of-scope items.

slides.title: Engineer implements
slides.body: The engineer works from the groomed issue and commits the implementation.

slides.title: QA verifies
slides.body: QA checks each acceptance criterion. The verdict is pass or fail, with specific failures when needed.

slides.title: Failures loop back
slides.body: If QA fails the work, the issue returns to the engineer. The orchestrator keeps the workflow moving.

slides.title: The trade-off
slides.body: This uses more tokens than one prompt. The benefit is better quality because QA often catches missed behavior.

slides.supportingText: Loop and graph engineering for coding-agent workflows.
